panels.title: Router cache locality
panels.description: The router's own view of prefix reuse, as two ratios that must be read apart. selected/query is what the chosen worker holds — the router's prediction of the engine's hit rate, and the only one comparable to the engine's sglang:cached_tokens_total / sglang:prompt_tokens_total. matched/query is the deepest prefix ANY worker in the fleet holds, so it reads structurally high: it counts selections that then routed elsewhere. The gap between the two lines is locality the routing decision gave up; the gap between selected/query and the engine's number is cache state that changed between selection and prefill. selected/query sitting BELOW the engine's rate is the third case and means a worker serves traffic while publishing no KV events — a failed /server_info probe or a page-size disagreement — not eviction. Kept per model_id: ratios are not additive across models.

panels.title: Cache-aware decisions
panels.description: Terminal outcome of every cache-aware selection, in the vocabulary of sgl_router_cache_aware_decisions_total. Evaluations, not requests — which is why the unit is not ops and the series are not stacked. cache_hit = a prefix owner won. cache_miss = no usable owner: a tree miss, no lookup at all, or every owner rejected by hard capacity admission. cache_worker_queued = the queue gate (--worker-queue-limit) diverted the request off its prefix while an unqueued worker existed. all_queued = the gate fired and no diversion could dodge a wait — a saturation signal, deliberately not spelled cache_hit*. Selections that ended in a 503 are absent, in sgl_router_policy_selection_failures_total instead. Rates are additive across models, so model_id is collapsed here.

panels.title: Locality by decision
panels.description: selected/query split by the decision that produced it — which bucket is losing the locality. A low ratio under cache_worker_queued is the queue gate trading prefix for a shorter wait; read it against sgl_router_diverted_overlap_blocks. A low ratio under cache_hit means the winner held little to begin with: read it with Router cache locality, where a matched/query that is also low says the fleet simply does not hold this traffic's prefixes. cache_miss usually reads near 0: it rises above 0 only when the fallback lands on a holder below the cache threshold. Kept per model_id: ratios are not additive across models.

targets.expr: sum by (model_id, decision) (rate(sgl_router_selected_overlap_blocks_total{model_id=~"$model_id"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (model_id, decision) (rate(sgl_router_cache_aware_query_blocks_total{model_id=~"$model_id"}[$__rate_interval])), 1e-9)

panels.title: Zero-match attribution
panels.description: Selections that matched nothing, split by whether the request's FIRST queried block hash exists anywhere in the tree. in_tree = the hash IS carried but the root-anchored walk could not reach it, so the work is router-side linkage. absent = no node carries it: never published, already removed, or held but never re-announced — a resident block is not re-published, so a router that started after the fleet was warm reads absent on a hot prefix indefinitely. Read absent against the KV tree vs engine coverage panel before blaming the engines. Emitted only where the in-process tree is the provider — an external Indexer cannot answer this, and the panel is empty there rather than wrong.

panels.title: Lookup availability — fleet vs worst replica
panels.description: Share of cache-aware selections that got a prefix lookup at all: selections that observed sgl_router_overlap_blocks over all selections in sgl_router_cache_aware_decisions_total. Both are booked at the same site for the same selections, so a healthy router reads 1. Every router replica maintains its own block-size oracle, so one replica can lose the lookup while the fleet aggregate stays healthy — the worst-replica line is the only place that shows. A replica below 1 has not yet learned the fleet's page size (or has no routing tokens for its traffic), and what it routes goes out blind. A lost KV subscription or a page-size change does NOT show here — lookups keep running and miss; read those on Router cache locality and Zero-match attribution. The numerator supplies an explicit zero, so a replica that never looked anything up reads 0 rather than dropping off; a replica or model with no traffic in the window has no denominator and drops out instead of reading 0.

targets.expr: min((sum without (decision) (rate(sgl_router_overlap_blocks_count{model_id=~"$model_id"}[$__rate_interval])) or sum without (decision) (rate(sgl_router_cache_aware_decisions_total{model_id=~"$model_id"}[$__rate_interval])) * 0) / (sum without (decision) (rate(sgl_router_cache_aware_decisions_total{model_id=~"$model_id"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0))

panels.title: Sticky-session outcomes
panels.description: hit / assigned / remap / no_routing_key.

panels.title: Decode-affinity outcomes
panels.description: same_host_picked / fallback_breaker / fallback_load_imbalance.

panels.title: Stale-request cancellations
panels.description: Stale-request cancellations fired by the janitor.

panels.title: KV event blocks by medium
panels.description: Blocks/s the router tree consumes, by event kind and the storage-medium tag the engine put on the event, per deployment. On a hierarchical-cache fleet block_stored/CPU_PINNED runs at roughly the block_removed/GPU rate; they are not equal, because the engine also evicts device blocks it never backed up. A CPU_PINNED line at 0 while the engines report hicache backups means the tier stream is not reaching the router. Both the busiest and the quietest replica are plotted: every replica receives the full stream, so a quietest-replica line at 0 while the busiest is healthy means one replica has lost its subscription and is routing blind.

panels.title: KV tree blocks by tier (fleet)
panels.description: Blocks the router tree attributes to the fleet, by the tier the worker holds them on (a block held on device and host counts under both). Absolute counts, so summing across workers is valid. host should sit at roughly hicache-ratio times device on a fleet with a full host tier; host at 0 means routing cannot see the L2 tier at all. max per worker across replicas, then summed.

panels.title: Tree coverage of engine host tier
panels.description: Router-attributed host-tier tokens / engine hicache host tokens in use, per deployment. ~1: every block the engines hold on host is routable. ~0 with a full host tier: the L2 tier is invisible to routing and repeats of anything evicted from device land on random pods -- this is the ratio that separates a retention problem (the engines really evicted it) from a visibility problem (the engines still hold it, the router forgot). Above 1: the tree holds tiers a worker already released, so check sgl_router_kv_event_batches_lost_total -- a tagged removal clears only its own tier, and a batch lost in transit strands the rest. Both sides are grouped by namespace because the ratio is not additive across deployments.

targets.expr: (sum by (namespace) (max by (namespace, worker_url, dp_rank) (sgl_router_kv_tree_blocks{tier="host"})) * on(namespace) group_left() max by (namespace) (sgl_router_kv_block_size)) / sum by (namespace) (sglang:hicache_host_used_tokens{tp_rank="0"})

panels.title: Cache hits by tier served from
panels.description: Which storage tier the CHOSEN worker holds the matched prefix on, in the same vocabulary as KV tree blocks by tier: device = served in place, host = served by a load-back from host memory, disk / external = fetched from a storage backend. Two labels are not tiers. none = the chosen worker holds no part of this prefix, usually a cache_miss or cache_worker_queued selection, or one whose winner was not an owner; a fallback that lands on a holder below the cache threshold reports that holder's tier instead. unknown = the deployment routes through the out-of-process Indexer, whose wire contract carries no medium — the tier is not observable there, and this reports so rather than defaulting to device.

panels.title: Affinity routes served by load-back
panels.description: host / (device + host): the fraction of in-place-or-load-back hits that ride the host tier rather than device HBM. This is what the storage-tier work buys, stated as a number — before the tree honoured tiers, every one of these was a cold prefill on a random worker instead. Rising is normal as device turns over (the device tier holds minutes, host holds hours); rising toward 1 while the engines report a healthy device pool means device ownership is being revoked faster than it should be. Kept per model_id: ratios are not additive across models.
